=== README.md
# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
=== migrations/001_create_users.sql
-- migration 001: create users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT
);
=== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));
=== schema.sql
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

arguments.command:
cat > migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql <<'EOF'
-- migration 003: drop notes
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
EOF
cat > schema.sql <<'EOF'
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
EOF
grep -rn notes --exclude-dir=.git . ; rm -f /tmp/t.db; for f in migrations/*.sql; do sqlite3 /tmp/t.db < $f || echo FAIL $f; done; sqlite3 /tmp/t.db .schema

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql`:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop notes
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also removed `notes` from `schema.sql`. The README says that file is kept in sync with the migrations by hand.

I ran migrations 001–003 in order against a fresh SQLite database with no errors, and the resulting schema matches the new `schema.sql`. No other code in the repo uses `notes`. I haven't committed anything.

**Before this deploys:** the deploy job runs migrations automatically, and production has about 48,000 rows in `users`. This will permanently delete whatever is in `notes` for all of them, and there's no down migration. If any of that data might be worth keeping, back up the column first (for example, `SELECT id, notes FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL`).

`DROP COLUMN` also needs SQLite 3.35 or newer on the production host.
